exercises.name: Long run
exercises.how_to: HR 140–150. No MP finish this week — just easy comfortable running. The goal is maintaining aerobic stimulus without adding fatigue ahead of taper.

days.name: Easy Run
days.description: 6 km easy.

days.name: Strength — Legs (Taper: 2 sets, −20%)
days.description: Taper mode: 2 sets each at ~80% of recent working weight. Maintain, don't build.

exercises.name: Single-leg RDL
exercises.how_to: −20% load. Maintain movement quality, not loading.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.how_to: −20% load. Freshen legs, not stress them.

exercises.name: Eccentric calf drop (step)
exercises.how_to: Reduced volume. Still important for tendon health pre-race.

days.name: Marathon Pace Run
days.description: 12 km total: 2 km easy + 8 km @ 4:00/km + 2 km easy. Maintain sharpness.

exercises.name: Marathon pace
exercises.how_to: HR 155–165. Controlled. This should feel easier than it did at peak week — that's taper working. Trust the training.

days.name: Easy Run + Upper Body
days.description: 8 km easy then upper body (2 sets, −20%).

exercises.name: DB shoulder press + Rear delt fly (superset)

days.name: Easy Run
days.description: 6 km easy.

days.name: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest. Off-day: eccentric calf drops × 15 each, hip hinge × 10, balance × 60s.

days.name: Long Run
days.description: 20 km easy. Volume drops significantly.

exercises.name: Long run
exercises.how_to: HR 140–150. Easy and comfortable. No MP finish. The reduced volume will feel strange — that's taper working, not detraining.

days.name: Easy Run
days.description: 6 km easy.

days.name: Strength — Legs (Taper: 2 sets, −20%)
days.description: Taper strength. Keep legs firing, don't fatigue them.

days.name: Easy Run + Strides
days.description: 8 km easy + 4 × 20s strides @ 3:20–3:30/km. Keep legs sharp.

exercises.name: Strides
exercises.how_to: In the last km, 4 controlled accelerations with full recovery between. Sharp and smooth. Keeps neuromuscular sharpness without adding fatigue — exactly what taper running needs.

days.name: Easy Run
days.description: 6 km easy.

days.name: Easy Run
days.description: 4 km easy. Volume dropping sharply now.

exercises.name: Easy run
exercises.how_to: HR < 145. Short run. The legs should feel fresh and springy by now — trust it.

days.name: Rest Day
days.description: Full rest. Off-day: eccentric calf drops × 15 each, hip hinge × 10, balance × 60s.

days.name: Easy Long Run
days.description: 14 km easy — no effort, no MP. Just moving.

exercises.name: Long run
exercises.how_to: HR 140–150. Easy and relaxed. This is the last long run before Frankfurt. No heroics — just comfortable movement to maintain aerobic feel.

days.name: Easy Run
days.description: 6 km easy.

days.name: Strength — Legs (Last Gym Session)
days.description: Last gym session. 2 sets, −20%. Don't add any fatigue this close to race day.

exercises.name: Single-leg RDL
exercises.how_to: −20% load. Last gym session before Frankfurt.

days.name: Easy Run + Strides
days.description: 5 km easy + 4 × 20s strides. Keep legs awake.

exercises.name: Strides
exercises.how_to: 4 short, controlled accelerations. Remind the legs what fast feels like. Full recovery between each.

days.name: Easy Run + Upper Body
days.description: 4 km easy + upper body (2 sets, −20%). Last structured training day.

exercises.name: DB shoulder press + Rear delt fly (superset)

days.name: Shakeout Run
days.description: 3 km easy — just to move. Legs should feel springy.

exercises.name: Shakeout
exercises.how_to: HR < 140. 3 easy km to keep the legs from stiffening. Include 2 × 20s strides at the end if legs feel flat. Nothing more.

days.name: Rest — Kit Prep
days.description: Full rest. Kit prep: pin on number, charge watch, set out Vaporflys, lay out gels, check start logistics.

days.name: Rest — Travel / Check-in
days.description: Travel to Frankfurt / check in / pasta dinner. Rest. Trust the training. It's done.

days.name: Frankfurt Marathon — Sub-2:50
days.description: Race day. 4:00/km. Even splits. First 5 km feel easy — that's correct. Race starts at 35 km.

exercises.name: Pre-race warmup
exercises.how_to: 10 min easy jog, leg swings, high knees, calf raises. Don't sprint the first km.

exercises.name: Km 1–10: Settle
exercises.how_to: Hold back. The first 10 km should feel controlled. HR will be elevated from adrenaline — trust pace, not feel.

exercises.name: Km 10–30: Execute
exercises.how_to: Take gels every 25 min. Stay even. If you feel great at 20 km, bank it — don't accelerate yet.

exercises.name: Km 30–35: Hold
exercises.how_to: This is where training counts. If calves feel tight, drop to 4:05–4:10/km — sub-2:52 still beats your PB.

exercises.name: Km 35–42.2: Finish
exercises.how_to: If you have anything left at 35 km, give it. The next 7 km are what the last 20 weeks built.
